heroHeadline: World Cup Final Set: Spain to Face Argentina Sunday at MetLife Stadium
heroSubtitle: The month since the group stage concluded produced a dramatic knockout run. Round of 32 upsets saw Paraguay eliminate Germany 4-3 on penalties and Morocco oust the Netherlands 3-2 on penalties (both June 29), while Argentina's Lionel Messi scored his 7th career World Cup goal in a 3-2 extra-time win over Cabo Verde (July 3). In the Round of 16, the United States was eliminated 1-4 by Belgium at Lumen Field, Seattle (July 6) in a match that drew a US-record 33.086 million Fox viewers — the most-watched soccer telecast in American history — and Argentina beat Egypt 3-2 (July 7) amid an officiating dispute that prompted Egypt's football association to say it 'cannot remain silent.' Quarterfinals (July 9-11) sent France, Spain, England, and Argentina through, with Kylian Mbappe suffering a 'minor ankle injury' in France's win over Morocco and FIFA changing its VAR staffing protocol for the semifinals after the officiating backlash. Spain beat France 2-0 in Dallas (July 14, Oyarzabal penalty + Porro), and Argentina rallied past England 2-1 in Atlanta (July 15) to set up the first-ever World Cup Final between Spain and Argentina — Sunday, July 19 at MetLife Stadium, New Jersey, kickoff 3:00 PM ET. France and England meet first in the third-place playoff, Saturday July 18 at Hard Rock Stadium, Miami.
